result.title: Adaptive Domain Decomposition for Finite Basis Physics-Informed Neural Networks
result.summary: In this work, we present adaptive domain decomposition finite basis physics-informed neural networks (ADD-FBPINNs). The proposed method integrates Partition of Unity Networks (POUNets), a data-driven approach for learning domain partitions, with finite Basis physics-informed neural networks (FBPINNs) to perform more efficient domain decomposition and achieve more accurate approximations. FBPINNs improve upon the accuracy of standard physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) through user-defined subdivisions of the computational domain. By adapting the domain decomposition based on the solution's features using a separable POUNet, the framework can automatically learn partitions that are stable and can be geometrically interpretable. We test this approach on the two-dimensional Helmholtz equation, two-dimensional Poisson equation with multiscale features, and viscous Burgers equation and observe improved accuracy compared with FBPINNs with fixed domain decomposition.

AI.brief_summary: 该工作将 POUNets 学习到的可分离域划分与有限基 PINNs 结合，提出 ADD-FBPINNs，在多个二维 PDE（Helmholtz、多尺度 Poisson、Burgers）上自动学习稳定且几何可解释的子域划分以提升精度。
